page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epdsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. The CPU architecture is arm64, with a cache configuration consisting of 64 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 128 MB L3 cache. The instance lacks hyperthreading, providing a single thread per core. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core, and includes a local 1890 GB NVMe SSD. No GPUs are present on this server.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 66297.85 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 20088.0. Memory performance is a key strength, as evidenced by top-tier results in large-block read-only memory bandwidth at 449.0 GB/sec and large-block write memory bandwidth at 188.31 GB/sec, alongside a top-tier Passmark memory score of 3327.28. Database operations are highly efficient, with Passmark database operations scoring in the top tier at 37819.86. Single-core performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2075.09.

While the server demonstrates strong capabilities in multi-threaded tasks, such as bzip3 decompression and software compilation, it exhibits limitations in large-scale machine learning workloads. Specifically, prompt processing for a large 70B LLM model is poor, registering at 4.65 tokens/sec, though text generation for the same model remains average at 3.08 tokens/sec. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, top-tier database operation benchmarks, and integrated NVMe SSD storage, this server is optimized for memory-intensive workloads, database management, static web serving, and multi-threaded software compilation.
